questions.question_text: Which data structure follows the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle?
questions.explanation: A stack operates on the LIFO principle, where the last element added is the first one removed.

questions.question_text: In binary representation, what is the decimal equivalent of 1011?
Which of these is a non-volatile memory?
questions.explanation: ROM (Read-Only Memory) retains its data even when power is turned off, unlike RAM.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of an Operating System?
questions.explanation: An OS acts as an interface between hardware and software, managing CPU, memory, and devices.

questions.question_text: In object-oriented programming, what is encapsulation?
options: Hiding internal state and requiring all interaction through methods
Inheriting properties from a base class
The ability for a method to have different behaviors
questions.explanation: Encapsulation restricts direct access to data to prevent accidental modification.

questions.question_text: Which layer of the OSI model handles logical addressing?
questions.explanation: The Network Layer is responsible for routing and logical addressing (IP addresses).

questions.question_text: Which SQL command is used to delete records from a table?
questions.explanation: The DELETE statement is used to remove existing rows from a table.

questions.question_text: What is the time complexity of searching for an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree?
questions.explanation: In a balanced Binary Search Tree, the height of the tree is log n, making the search time proportional to the height.

questions.question_text: Which protocol is used to securely transfer files over a network?
questions.explanation: SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) provides secure, encrypted file transfers.

questions.question_text: What does the 'TCP' in TCP/IP stand for?
questions.explanation: TCP is a core protocol of the Internet Protocol suite providing reliable, ordered delivery of data.
